changes: Purpose rephrased: 'śrīrājapustakaṃ' marks the copy as the king's book (unnamed royal owner); it is not a purpose formula. No person added because no king is named.
Date: nakṣatra 1 interpreted as Aśvinī; as_written now includes the unclear 'jitā (!)'.
Notes expanded: scribe-name reading, 'jitā (!)', and that no era or year is given.

purpose: royal copy (śrīrājapustakaṃ: the king's book; king not named)
notes: The scribe's name 'rāmahadvuja' is probably a corruption of 'Rāmabhadradvija' (Rāmabhadra, a dvija). The cataloguer's 'Rāmabhadradvuja' supports this. 'jitā (!)' is unclear: it may be a corrupted date element or the end of a dating formula. 'śrīrājapustakaṃ' marks the manuscript as belonging to an unnamed king, so no royal person can be recorded. The date gives only month 10, nakṣatra 1 and tithi 11, with no year or era, so no CE date can be worked out. The colophon ends the Uñchavṛtti-upākhyāna of the Mokṣadharma section (Śāntiparvan).
